name: qdrant-managed-cloud-quickstart-offboarding-billing
prompt: A contractor set up our Qdrant Cloud account last spring, and we removed them from the account when they left last month. This week our nightly CI job started getting 401s from the production cluster. It uses a Database API key the contractor created around three months ago. Separately, finance wants us to pay through the AWS Marketplace from now on, and we're also planning to add a cluster on GCP for a team that lives there. How should we sort all this out?

rubric.text: Flags that removing the contractor from the account did not revoke the keys they created: their Database API keys and any Cloud Management Keys keep working with the permissions they were granted, and must be revoked separately
Says to check whether the CI key has expired, since Database API keys expire after 90 days by default and this one is about three months old, and to replace it with a new key
Explains that paying through the AWS Marketplace limits the account to paid clusters in AWS regions, so the GCP cluster needs a separate account with a different payment method
Suggests checking IP restrictions on the cluster as another possible cause of the CI failures, if the CI runners' addresses changed
Recommends setting a deliberate expiration on the replacement key and rotating keys regularly
States or implies that removing a user from the account revokes the API keys they created
States or implies that a single Marketplace-billed account can run clusters on both AWS and GCP
